title: Optional NIP-86 managed relay administration
observed_behavior_before: Bahia documented NIP-86 as optional relay-owner administration but had no opt-in configuration model for managed relay targets.
There was no isolated NIP-86 HTTP client that required NIP-98 payload-bound authorization and rejected non-NIP-86 application/control-plane methods.
Existing NIP-42 websocket AUTH work is owned by bahia-8epx.7 and must not be replaced by HTTP relay administration.
intended_behavior: NIP-86 relay administration remains disabled by default with no configured targets.

Enabling relay administration requires an administrator private-key secret reference and explicitly Bahia-owned or Bahia-authorized target relays with secure relay/admin URLs and allowed administrator pubkeys.

The NIP-86 client sends only relay-owner administration methods over HTTP, signs every request with NIP-98 kind 27235, and includes the SHA-256 hash of the exact JSON request body in the required payload tag.
The client refuses disabled, unconfigured, administrator-pubkey-mismatched, HTTP-error, relay-error, and non-NIP-86 ContextVM/application method paths deterministically.
out_of_scope: Changing NIP-42 websocket AUTH behavior in existing relay clients.
Routing ContextVM kind 25910 app/control-plane mutations through NIP-86.
Adding a UI, CLI command, or automatic relay policy reconciler for relay administration.
NIP-11, NIP-66, and NIP-51 10050 DM relay-list implementation slices.
